image_description: A disassembled bassoon lying on a concrete surface, partially resting on a dark fabric case. The visible sections include the boot joint and wing joint with complex metal keywork. The bell section is visible at the bottom-left, flaring outward. The wood is reddish-brown with white binding tape. The instrument is not assembled into its playing U-shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long wooden wind instrument of considerable height when assembled.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument is disassembled and lying horizontally; the full assembled height cannot be verified from this view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinctive U-shape when viewed from front with bell pointing upward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The instrument is not assembled into its playing U-shape; it is in separate sections lying flat.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Conical bore that doubles back on itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Internal bore structure is not visible externally, and the doubling-back geometry is only apparent when assembled.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Curved metal bocal mouthpiece tube at top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bocal (mouthpiece) is not visible in the image; it may be missing or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Numerous metal keys and tone holes distributed along length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple silver-colored metal keys, rods, and tone holes are clearly visible along the wooden body sections.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bell flares outward at top and instrument held diagonally across body when played.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bell section is clearly visible at the bottom-left of the image. It exhibits the characteristic outward flare of a bassoon bell. The 'held diagonally' part is not applicable as it is lying down, but the component presence is confirmed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark reddish-brown polished wood finish maple or rosewood.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wooden sections exhibit a reddish-brown color consistent with stained maple or rosewood used for bassoons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal keys are silver or gold-plated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visible keywork appears silver-colored, consistent with nickel-silver or silver-plated metal.
The visible sections are clearly constructed from turned wooden tubes with metal fittings.

artifact_observations.location: Key rod connections and mounting posts on lower joint
artifact_observations.reasoning: Significant mechanical implausibility: several key rods appear to merge directly into the wood without visible mounting posts or screws. Some keys lack logical pivot points or connecting springs, appearing to float or fuse with the body. This is a hallmark AI artifact where complex mechanical assemblies are approximated rather than structurally defined.

artifact_observations.location: Wooden body surface near key mounts
artifact_observations.reasoning: Wood grain texture becomes unnaturally smooth and smudged around the base of the metal keys, lacking the crisp boundary expected between polished wood and metal fittings. Suggests generative blending errors.

artifact_observations.location: Edges of fabric case and background concrete
artifact_observations.reasoning: Mild blurring at boundaries between the instrument/case and the concrete floor, typical of depth-of-field simulation but slightly uneven.

selected_experts.reason: Verify that the object is indeed a bassoon and not a similar woodwind based on key layout and proportions.
Audit connectivity between metal keys/rods and wooden body to ensure no floating parts, fused elements, or impossible attachments. Specifically check for mechanical plausibility of the key system.
Assess overall realism, lighting consistency, and detect subtle generative artifacts in textures and edges.
Verify spatial grounding of the instrument on the concrete surface and check for depth inconsistencies between overlapping parts.

focus_areas: Mechanical Logic Audit: Verify every visible key has a corresponding rod, spring, or pad, and that no keys float in mid-air or merge into the wood body.
Key mechanism attachment points and physical plausibility (mounting posts/screws)
Wood grain texture consistency and realism at metal-wood boundaries
Boundary sharpness between instrument, case, and background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Critically evaluate the mechanical plausibility of the keywork. Look for 'melted' keys where rods pass through wood without mounting posts, or keys that lack logical pivot points. Check if the wood grain looks procedurally generated vs. natural, especially near the keys. Verify that the bell section is correctly shaped and connected. Do not rubber-stamp the Router's severity ratings; if keys look physically impossible, increase the artifact severity.
